entries.sanskrit:
विंशे वराह-जन्मादि- व्यवधानाद् अथादितः ।

सर्गोऽनुस्मार्यते वक्तुम् अन्वयं प्रस्तुतां मनोः ॥

प्रतिष्ठां स्थानम् । अध्यस्य प्राप्य । सौते सूतस्य रोमहर्षणस्य पुत्र । अवरम् अर्वाचीनं जन्म येषां तेषाम् ईश्वरे लीनानां मार्गाय निर्गमाय कानि द्वाराणि कृतवान् ? अर्वाचीनान् प्राणिनः कैर् उपायैः सृष्टवान् ? इत्य् अर्थः ॥१॥
word_for_word: विंशे
in the twentieth [chapter]
वराह-जन्मादि- व्यवधानाद् अथादितः
then, from the beginning, after the interruption caused by the account beginning with Varāha’s birth
सर्गोऽनुस्मार्यते वक्तुम्
creation is recalled in order to tell
अन्वयं प्रस्तुतां मनोः
the lineage of Manu now being introduced
प्रतिष्ठां स्थानम्
“pratiṣṭhā” means a place or abode
अध्यस्य प्राप्य
“adhyasya” means having reached or obtained
सौते सूतस्य रोमहर्षणस्य पुत्र
“O Sūta” means son of Sūta Romaharṣaṇa
अवरम् अर्वाचीनं जन्म येषां तेषाम्
“later” means those whose births are subsequent
ईश्वरे लीनानां मार्गाय निर्गमाय कानि द्वाराणि कृतवान्
for the passage out of those absorbed in the Lord, what doors did he make?
अर्वाचीनान् प्राणिनः कैर् उपायैः सृष्टवान् ? इत्य् अर्थः
By what means did he create later creatures? This is the meaning.
entries.literal_english: In the twentieth chapter, after the interruption caused by the account beginning with Varāha’s birth, creation is recalled from the beginning so that Manu’s genealogy, now being introduced, may be told. “Pratiṣṭhā” means a place or abode; “adhyasya” means having reached or obtained it. “O Sūta” means the son of Romaharṣaṇa. “Later-born” means those whose births are subsequent. For the passage out of their absorption in the Lord, what doors did Manu make? By what means did he create later creatures? That is the meaning.

entries.sanskrit: विदुर-मैत्रेय-संवादेनैवैतज् ज्ञास्यत इति तम् एव संवादं प्रष्टुम् आह---क्षत्तेति पञ्चभिः । श्री-कृष्ण-सुहृत्त्वे हेतुः---य इति । दुर्योधनादिभिर् अपत्यैः सहितम् अग्रजं धृतराष्ट्रम् अघवान् कृतापराध इति हेतोः श्री-कृष्णोक्त-मन्त्रानादरात् यस् तत्याज ॥२॥ अनवरोऽन्यूनः । महित्वे महिम्नि ॥३॥ कुशावर्ते गङ्गा-द्वारे ॥४॥
word_for_word: विदुर-मैत्रेय-संवादेनैवैतज् ज्ञास्यत इति
because this will indeed be known through the dialogue between Vidura and Maitreya
तम् एव संवादं प्रष्टुम् आह---क्षत्तेति पञ्चभिः
to ask about that very dialogue, he says “kṣattā” in five verses
श्री-कृष्ण-सुहृत्त्वे हेतुः---य इति
“yaḥ” states the reason for friendship with Śrī Kṛṣṇa
दुर्योधनादिभिर् अपत्यैः सहितम् अग्रजं धृतराष्ट्रम्
his elder brother Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with sons such as Duryodhana
अघवान् कृतापराध इति हेतोः
because he was sinful, having committed an offense
श्री-कृष्णोक्त-मन्त्रानादरात् यस् तत्याज
he abandoned him because of disregard for Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s counsel
अनवरोऽन्यूनः
“anavara” means not inferior, undiminished
महित्वे महिम्नि
“mahitve” means in greatness
कुशावर्ते गङ्गा-द्वारे
Kuśāvarta is at Gaṅgā-dvāra
entries.literal_english: Because this will be known through the dialogue between Vidura and Maitreya, he asks to hear that very dialogue, saying “kṣattā” in five verses. “Yaḥ” gives the reason for Vidura’s friendship with Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Vidura abandoned his elder brother Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with sons such as Duryodhana, because Dhṛtarāṣṭra was sinful and had committed an offense by disregarding Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s counsel. “Anavara” means not inferior or undiminished; “mahitve” means in greatness; Kuśāvarta is at Gaṅgā-dvāra.

ब्रह्मा किम् आरभतेति प्रश्नस्य यक्षादीन् सृष्टवान् इत्य् उत्तरं वक्तुं पूर्वोक्तां सृष्टिम् अनुस्मारयति, दैवेनेति सप्तभिः । मन्व्-आदि-प्रश्नानां तूत्तराध्यायम् आरभोत्तरं भविष्यति । दुर्वितर्क्येण दैवेन जीवादृष्टेन, परेण प्रकृत्य्-अधिष्ठात्रा महा-पुरुषेणानिमिषेण कालेन च हेतुना भगवतो निविङ्काराज् जात-क्षोभं यद् गुण-त्रयं प्रधानं तस्मान् महान् आसीत् । तद् उक्तं तन्त्रे---
विष्णोस् तु त्रीणि रूपाणि पुरुषाख्यान्य् अथो विदुः । प्रथमं महतः स्रष्टृ द्वितीयं त्व् अण्ड-संस्थितम् । तृतीयं सर्व-भूत-स्थं तानि ज्ञात्वा विमुच्यते ॥ इति ॥१२॥
word_for_word: ब्रह्मा किम् आरभतेति प्रश्नस्य यक्षादीन् सृष्टवान् इत्य् उत्तरं वक्तुं पूर्वोक्तां सृष्टिम् अनुस्मारयति, दैवेनेति सप्तभिः
to answer the question “What did Brahmā undertake?”—that he created Yakṣas and others—he recalls the preceding creation in seven verses beginning “daivena”
मन्व्-आदि-प्रश्नानां तूत्तराध्यायम् आरभोत्तरं भविष्यति
the questions concerning Manu and the rest will be answered beginning in the next chapter
दुर्वितर्क्येण दैवेन जीवादृष्टेन, परेण प्रकृत्य्-अधिष्ठात्रा महा-पुरुषेणानिमिषेण कालेन च हेतुना भगवतो निविङ्काराज् जात-क्षोभं यद् गुण-त्रयं प्रधानं तस्मान् महान् आसीत्

from the Lord’s unmodified nature, agitated by inscrutable providence (the living being’s unseen karma), the Supreme Person presiding over primordial nature, and time, arose the three qualities called pradhāna; from them arose Mahat
तद् उक्तं तन्त्रे
this is stated in the Tantra
विष्णोस् तु त्रीणि रूपाणि पुरुषाख्यान्य् अथो विदुः । प्रथमं महतः स्रष्टृ द्वितीयं त्व् अण्ड-संस्थितम् । तृतीयं सर्व-भूत-स्थं तानि ज्ञात्वा विमुच्यते ॥ इति
“They know Viṣṇu’s three forms, called Puruṣas: the first creates Mahat, the second is situated in the cosmic egg, and the third is present in all beings; knowing these, one is liberated.”
entries.literal_english: To answer the question “What did Brahmā undertake?”—that he created the Yakṣas and others—the preceding creation is recalled with “daivena” in seven verses. The questions concerning Manu and the rest will be answered in the next chapter. From the Lord’s unmodified nature, agitated by inscrutable providence (the unseen karma of the living being), by the Supreme Person who presides over primordial nature, and by time (the Unblinking Lord), there arose the three qualities, called pradhāna, and from them Mahat. This is stated in the Tantra: “They know the three forms of Viṣṇu, called Puruṣas: first, the creator of Mahat; second, situated within the cosmic egg; third, present in all beings. Knowing these, one is liberated.”

entries.sanskrit: महतो जातो भूतादिर् अहङ्कारस् त्रि-लिङ्गस् त्रि-गुणः । रजः प्रधानाद् इति स्वतः सत्त्व-प्रधानस्यापि महतोऽहङ्कारोत्पत्ति-काले कार्यानुरूपं रजः-प्रधानत्वं भवतीति भावः । पञ्चशः तन् मात्राणि मह-भूतानि ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि कर्मेन्द्रियाणि तत् तद् देवताश् चेति पञ्च ससर्जेत्य् अर्थः ॥१३॥

from Mahat arose bhūtādi, ahaṅkāra, marked by three characteristics and constituted of the three qualities
रजः प्रधानाद् इति
“predominant in rajas” means
स्वतः सत्त्व-प्रधानस्यापि महतोऽहङ्कारोत्पत्ति-काले कार्यानुरूपं रजः-प्रधानत्वं भवतीति भावः

पञ्चशः तन् मात्राणि मह-भूतानि ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि कर्मेन्द्रियाणि तत् तद् देवताश् चेति पञ्च ससर्जेत्य् अर्थः
“fivefold” means the subtle elements, great elements, cognitive senses, active senses, and their respective deities: five classes were created
entries.literal_english: From Mahat arose bhūtādi, ahaṅkāra, marked by three characteristics and constituted of the three qualities. “Predominant in rajas” means that, although sattva naturally predominates in Mahat, at the time ahaṅkāra arises rajas predominates in accordance with the effect. “Fivefold” means that he created five classes: the subtle elements, the great elements, the cognitive senses, the active senses, and their respective presiding deities.

entries.sanskrit: भौतिकं हैमम् अण्डम् एकैकशः प्रत्य् एकं स्रष्टुम् असमर्थानि सन्ति संहत्य ससृजुः ॥१४॥
word_for_word: भौतिकं हैमम् अण्डम्
the material, golden cosmic egg
एकैकशः प्रत्य् एकं स्रष्टुम् असमर्थानि सन्ति
being unable, each separately, to create individually
संहत्य ससृजुः
they combined and created [it]
entries.literal_english: The material, golden cosmic egg: since the [elements], each separately, were unable to create, they combined and created it.

entries.sanskrit: सहस्रार्काणाम् इवोरुर् दीधितिर् यस्य तत् । सर्व-जीवनिकायानाम् ओकः स्थानं पद्मम् । स्वराट् ब्रह्मा ॥१६॥

that which has immense radiance like a thousand suns
सर्व-जीवनिकायानाम् ओकः स्थानं पद्मम्
the lotus is the abode, the dwelling place, of all groups of living beings
स्वराट् ब्रह्मा
“svarāṭ” means Brahmā
entries.literal_english: “That which has immense radiance like a thousand suns.” The lotus is the abode, the dwelling place, of all groups of living beings. “Svarāṭ” means Brahmā.

entries.sanskrit: यः सलिलाशये गर्भोदकस्यान्तः शेते, तेन भगवतानुविष्टोऽधिष्ठितः सन्, स स्वराट् । स्वया संस्थया नाम-रूपादि-क्रमेण ॥१७॥
word_for_word: यः  सलिलाशये गर्भोदकस्यान्तः शेते
he who lies within the body of water, within the Garbhodaka
तेन भगवतानुविष्टोऽधिष्ठितः सन्, स स्वराट्
being entered and presided over by that Bhagavān, he is “svarāṭ”
स्वया संस्थया नाम-रूपादि-क्रमेण
“by his own constitution” means according to the sequence of name, form, and so forth
entries.literal_english: He who lies within the body of water, within the Garbhodaka, is entered and presided over by that Bhagavān. “Svarāṭ” [means Brahmā]. “By his own constitution” means according to the sequence of name, form, and so forth.

entries.sanskrit: छाया प्रभा-प्रतियोगिनी तया । अबुध्येत्य् अर्थः, यस् त्व् अबुद्धि-कृतः प्रभोः[भा।पु। ३.१०.१७] इत्य् उक्तत्वात् । महा-तम इति महा-मोहः । स्वरूप-निर्देश-मात्र-विवक्षया मोह इति प्रथमा-प्रयोगः ॥१८॥
word_for_word: छाया प्रभा-प्रतियोगिनी तया
“chāyā” is the counterpart of radiance; by that [shadow]
अबुध्येत्य् अर्थः, यस् त्व् अबुद्धि-कृतः प्रभोः[भा।पु। ३.१०.१७] इत्य् उक्तत्वात्
“he became bewildered”—this is the meaning, since it is said, “that which was produced from the Lord’s ignorance” (Bhāgavata 3.10.17)
महा-तम इति महा-मोहः
“great darkness” means great delusion
स्वरूप-निर्देश-मात्र-विवक्षया मोह इति प्रथमा-प्रयोगः
the nominative “moha” is used merely to designate the nature [of the state]
entries.literal_english: “Chāyā” is the counterpart or opposite of radiance (prabhā); by that [shadow] he became bewildered—this is the meaning, since it is said, “that which was produced from the Lord’s ignorance.” “Great darkness” means great delusion. The nominative form “moha” is used merely to designate the nature [of the state].
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.२०.18 from pinned source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं प्रथमोक्तां साधारणां सृष्टिम् अनूद्य केनचिद् विशेषेणासाधारणां सृष्टिम् आह---विससर्जेत्य्-आदिना यावत् समाप्ति । तद् विसृष्टं कायं रात्रि-रूपं तत एव जातानि यक्ष-रक्षांसि जगृहुः । क्षुत्-तृषोः समुद्भवो यस्यां ताम् । अत्र च, यास्य सा तनूर् आसीत् ताम् अपाहत सा तमिस्राभवत् इत्य्-आदि-श्रुतिर् अनुसन्धेया ॥१९॥
word_for_word: तद् एवं प्रथमोक्तां साधारणां सृष्टिम् अनूद्य
having restated the general creation described first
केनचिद् विशेषेणासाधारणां सृष्टिम् आह---विससर्जेत्य्-आदिना यावत् समाप्ति
he describes a particular, exceptional creation, beginning with “visasarja” and continuing to the end
तद् विसृष्टं कायं रात्रि-रूपं तत एव जातानि यक्ष-रक्षांसि जगृहुः
the body thus emitted in the form of night was seized by the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas born from it
क्षुत्-तृषोः समुद्भवो यस्यां ताम्
that [body] in which hunger and thirst arose
अत्र च, यास्य सा तनूर् आसीत् ताम् अपाहत सा तमिस्राभवत् इत्य्-आदि-श्रुतिर् अनुसन्धेया
here one should recall the Śruti beginning, “That body which was to be cast off, she cast away; it became darkness,” and so forth
entries.literal_english: Having restated the general creation described first, he now describes a particular, exceptional creation, beginning with “visasarja” and continuing to the end. The body thus emitted, in the form of night, was seized by the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas born from it. It was a body in which hunger and thirst arose. Here one should recall the Śruti beginning, “That body which was to be cast off, she cast away; it became darkness,” and so forth.

entries.sanskrit: उपसृष्टा अभिभूताः । जग्धुम् अत्तुं भक्षयितुम् । यतो वयं क्षुत्-तृड्भ्याम् अर्दिता अत एनं पितेति कृपया मा रक्षतेत्य् एके । अन्ये तु जक्षध्वं भक्षयतेति ब्रुवन्तः । जक्ष भक्ष-हसनयोर् इति धातुः ॥२०॥
word_for_word: उपसृष्टा अभिभूताः
“upasṛṣṭāḥ” means afflicted or overwhelmed
जग्धुम् अत्तुं भक्षयितुम्
“jagdhum” means to eat, consume, or devour
यतो वयं क्षुत्-तृड्भ्याम् अर्दिता अत एनं पितेति कृपया मा रक्षतेत्य् एके
some said, “Since we are afflicted by hunger and thirst, therefore, out of compassion, protect us, Father”
अन्ये तु जक्षध्वं भक्षयतेति ब्रुवन्तः
others said, “Eat! Devour!”
जक्ष भक्ष-हसनयोर् इति धातुः
the root jakṣ means eating or laughing
entries.literal_english: “Upasṛṣṭāḥ” means afflicted or overwhelmed; “jagdhum” means to eat, consume, or devour. Some said, “Since we are afflicted by hunger and thirst, therefore, out of compassion, protect us, Father.” Others said, “Eat! Devour!” The verbal root jakṣ means eating or laughing.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.२०.20 from pinned source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.
transliteration: upasṛṣṭā abhibhūtāḥ | jagdhum attuṃ bhakṣayitum | yato vayaṃ kṣut-tṛḍbhyām arditā ata enaṃ piteti kṛpayā mā rakṣatety eke | anye tu jakṣadhvaṃ bhakṣayateti bruvantaḥ | jakṣa bhakṣa-hasanayor iti dhātuḥ ||20||

entries.sanskrit: देवो ब्रह्मा संविग्नो भीतः सन् मां मा जक्षत मा भक्षयत, किन्तु रक्षत । अहो हे यक्ष-रक्षांसि, यूयं मे प्रजाः सुता बभूविथ जाताः स्थ । एवम् उग्र-स्वभावा यक्ष-राक्षसा जाता इत्य् अर्थः । तत्र ये जक्षध्वम् इत्य् ऊचुस् ते यक्षाः, ये तु मा रक्षतेति ते राक्षसा इति ज्ञेयम् । एतच् च तिर्यग्-आदि-तामस-सर्गस्याप्य् उपलक्षणम् ॥२१॥
word_for_word: देवो ब्रह्मा संविग्नो भीतः सन्
the lord Brahmā, distressed and afraid
मां मा जक्षत मा भक्षयत, किन्तु रक्षत
“Do not eat me, do not devour me, but protect me”
अहो हे यक्ष-रक्षांसि, यूयं मे प्रजाः सुता बभूविथ जाताः स्थ
“Ah, O Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, you have become my offspring”
एवम् उग्र-स्वभावा यक्ष-राक्षसा जाता इत्य् अर्थः
thus the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas were born with fierce natures; this is the meaning
तत्र ये जक्षध्वम् इत्य् ऊचुस् ते यक्षाः, ये तु मा रक्षतेति ते राक्षसा इति ज्ञेयम्
those who said “Eat!” are known as Yakṣas, and those who said “Protect us!” as Rākṣasas
एतच् च तिर्यग्-आदि-तामस-सर्गस्याप्य् उपलक्षणम्
this also indicates the tamasic creation of animals and the like
entries.literal_english: Frightened, the lord Brahmā said, “Do not eat me; do not devour me, but protect me. Ah, O Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, you have become my offspring.” Thus the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas were born with fierce natures. Those who said “Eat!” are known as Yakṣas; those who said “Protect us!” are known as Rākṣasas. This also indicates the tamasic creation of animals and the like.

entries.sanskrit: प्रभया दीव्यन् द्योतमानः । या या देवता द्युतिमत्यः सात्त्विक्यस् तास् ताः प्रमुखतः प्राधान्येनासृजत् । ते देवाः । देवता इति स्त्रीत्वेन निर्दिष्टानाम् अप्य् अर्थ-मात्र-विवक्षया त इति पुंस्त्वेन प्रतिनिर्देशः । एवं यक्ष-रक्षांसीत्य् अत्रापि ज्ञेयम् । तेन विसृष्टां त्यक्तां प्रभाम् अहः दिवस-रूपां सतीं देवयन्तः क्रीडयन्तोऽहार्षुर् जगृहुः॥२२॥
word_for_word: प्रभया दीव्यन् द्योतमानः
“shining with radiance” means resplendent
या या देवता द्युतिमत्यः सात्त्विक्यस् तास् ताः प्रमुखतः प्राधान्येनासृजत्
he created chiefly and prominently each of the luminous, sattvic deities
ते देवाः
“those are the gods”
देवता इति स्त्रीत्वेन निर्दिष्टानाम् अप्य् अर्थ-मात्र-विवक्षया त इति पुंस्त्वेन प्रतिनिर्देशः
although “devatā” is feminine, they are referred to by the masculine “they” because only the meaning is intended
एवं यक्ष-रक्षांसीत्य् अत्रापि ज्ञेयम्
the same is to be understood for “Yakṣas and Rākṣasas”
तेन विसृष्टां त्यक्तां प्रभाम् अहः दिवस-रूपां सतीं देवयन्तः क्रीडयन्तोऽहार्षुर् जगृहुः
sporting, they took the radiance he had cast off, which had become the form of day
entries.literal_english: “Shining with radiance” means resplendent. He created, chiefly and prominently, each of the luminous, sattvic deities. “Those are the gods.” Although the word devatā is grammatically feminine, they are referred to in the masculine as “they” because only the meaning is intended; the same is to be understood for “Yakṣas and Rākṣasas.” They sportively took the radiance that he had cast off, which had become the form of day.

entries.sanskrit: अदेवान् इति च्छेदः । स जघनाद् असुरान् असृजत इति श्रुतेः । अति-लोलुपान् स्त्री-लम्पटान् । अभिपेदिरे प्राप्ताः ॥२३॥
word_for_word: अदेवान् इति च्छेदः
the division is “a-devān,” “non-gods”
स जघनाद् असुरान् असृजत इति श्रुतेः
because the Śruti says, “He created the Asuras from his loins”
अति-लोलुपान् स्त्री-लम्पटान्
“ati-lolupān” means exceedingly greedy and lustful toward women
अभिपेदिरे प्राप्ताः
“abhipedire” means they approached
entries.literal_english: “Adevān” should be divided as “a-devān,” “non-gods,” because the Śruti says, “He created the Asuras from his loins.” “Ati-lolupān” means exceedingly greedy and lustful toward women. “Abhipedire” means they approached.

entries.sanskrit: भक्तेच्छानुरूपम् आत्मानं दर्शयतीति तथा तम् उपव्रज्य ॥२५॥

entries.sanskrit: विविक्तम् असन्दिग्धम् अध्यात्म-दर्शनं पर-चित्त-ज्ञानं यस्य हरेः । घोरां काम-कश्मलां स्व-तनुं विमुञ्चेति उक्तवान् इति शेषः । इत्य् उक्तश् च ब्रह्मा तं तनुं विमुमोच । सर्वत्र तनु-त्यागो नाम तत् तन् मनो-भाव-त्यागो विवक्षितः । ग्रहणं च तत् तद् भावापत्तिर् इति द्रष्टव्यम् ॥२८॥
word_for_word: विविक्तम् असन्दिग्धम् अध्यात्म-दर्शनं पर-चित्त-ज्ञानं यस्य हरेः

entries.literal_english: Hari is one whose inner vision is clear and free from doubt, whose knowledge of the self includes knowledge of others’ minds. “Give up your dreadful body, polluted by desire”—this is understood as what he told Brahmā. Having been told this, Brahmā gave up that body. In every such case, giving up a body means giving up the corresponding mental disposition; taking on a body means entering that corresponding state.

entries.sanskrit: साहो-रात्रयोः सन्धिर् अभवत् इति श्रुतेः । सा तेन विसृष्टा तनुः सायन्तनी सन्ध्या बभूव । सा च कामोद्रेक-वेला । असुराश् च राजसत्वात् स्त्री-लम्पटाः । अतस् तां सन्ध्याम् एव स्त्रियं कल्पयित्वा ते संमोहं प्राप्ता इत्य् आह---ताम् इति त्रिभिः । नूपुराभ्यां क्वणती चरणाम्भोजे यस्याः । मदेन विह्वले लोचने यस्याः । काञ्ची-कलापेन विलसद्-दुकूलं तेन छन्नं रोधः कटितटं यस्यास् ताम् ॥२९॥
word_for_word: साहो-रात्रयोः सन्धिर् अभवत् इति श्रुतेः
according to the Śruti, “the junction of day and night came to be”
सा तेन विसृष्टा तनुः सायन्तनी सन्ध्या बभूव
the body he cast off became the evening twilight
सा च कामोद्रेक-वेला
and that is the time when desire intensifies
असुराश् च राजसत्वात् स्त्री-लम्पटाः
the Asuras are rajasic and lustful toward women
अतस् तां सन्ध्याम् एव स्त्रियं कल्पयित्वा ते संमोहं प्राप्ता इत्य् आह---ताम् इति त्रिभिः
therefore, imagining twilight itself to be a woman, they became bewildered; this is stated in three verses beginning “tām”
नूपुराभ्यां क्वणती चरणाम्भोजे यस्याः
her lotus feet rang with her anklets
मदेन विह्वले लोचने यस्याः
her eyes were bewildered by intoxication
काञ्ची-कलापेन विलसद्-दुकूलं तेन छन्नं रोधः कटितटं यस्यास् ताम्
her hips were covered by shining silk, adorned with a girdle
entries.literal_english: According to the Śruti, “the junction of day and night came to be.” The body he cast off became the evening twilight, the time when desire intensifies. Since the Asuras are rajasic and lustful toward women, they imagined that twilight itself was a woman and became bewildered; this is stated in three verses beginning “tām.” Her lotus feet rang with her anklets; her eyes were bewildered by intoxication; her hips, adorned with a girdle and shining silk, were covered.

entries.sanskrit: कासीति त्रिभिः । कासि जात्या । कस्य वा कन्या ? हे भामिनि कोपने । रूपम् एव द्रविणम् अनर्घ्यं वस्तु । तद् एव पण्यं क्रयार्हम् । तेन तद्-असमर्पणेन नो विबाधसे ॥३४॥
word_for_word: कासीति त्रिभिः
the explanation beginning with “kāsi” spans three verses
कासि जात्या । कस्य वा कन्या
“kāsi” means “of what birth are you?” or “whose daughter?”
हे भामिनि कोपने
“bhāmini” means an angry or passionate woman
रूपम् एव द्रविणम् अनर्घ्यं वस्तु
her beauty itself is priceless wealth, an incomparable thing
तद् एव पण्यं क्रयार्हम्
it alone is merchandise fit to be bought
तेन तद्-असमर्पणेन नो विबाधसे
by withholding it, you distress us

Her beauty itself is priceless wealth, an incomparable thing; it alone is the merchandise fit to be bought. By withholding it, you distress us.

entries.sanskrit: किं जाति-कुलादि-प्रश्नेन या वा काचिद् भव । दिष्ट्या इदं तावद् भद्रं जातं यत् तव दर्शनम् । किन्तु केवलं नो मन उत्सुनोषि विमथ्नासि ॥३५॥
word_for_word: किं जाति-कुलादि-प्रश्नेन या वा काचिद् भव

entries.literal_english: “What is the use of asking about birth, family, and the like? Whoever you may be, fortunately at least this has happened: we have seen you. Yet you alone agitate and churn our minds.”

entries.sanskrit: क्षुभित-चित्तानां वाक्यं नैकत्रेति । हे शालिनि श्लाध्ये । एकत्र न जयति न स्थिरी-भवति । यद् वा, नैकत्रानेक-गति-विलासेषु जयति सर्वोत्कर्षेण वर्तते । पतत्-पतङ्गम् उच्छलन्तं कन्दुकम् । बृहतोः स्तनयोर् भाराद् भीतं तव कृशं मध्यं विषीदति श्राम्यति । शान्ता मन्थरेव प्रसरति । सु-शिखा-समूहः शोभनः केश-कलापस् ते । पाठान्तरे सुशिखाः शोभनान् केशान् अवकीर्यमाणान् समूहः बधानेति । अत्र चास्तं गच्छन् सूर्य एव पतत्-पतङ्गः, मेघ-विच्छेदो मध्य-विषादः तारका-रूपा दृष्टिः, तम एव केशा इत्य्-आद्य्-ऊह्यम् ॥३६॥
word_for_word: क्षुभित-चित्तानां वाक्यं नैकत्रेति
because the words of their agitated minds do not stay on one subject
हे शालिनि श्लाध्ये
“O graceful woman, O praiseworthy one”
एकत्र न जयति न स्थिरी-भवति
“it does not stay in one place; it does not become steady”
यद् वा, नैकत्रानेक-गति-विलासेषु जयति सर्वोत्कर्षेण वर्तते
or, amid many varied graceful motions, it excels everywhere
पतत्-पतङ्गम् उच्छलन्तं कन्दुकम्
“a falling ball” means a ball bouncing upward
बृहतोः स्तनयोर् भाराद् भीतं तव कृशं मध्यं विषीदति श्राम्यति
your slender waist, burdened by your large breasts, droops and grows weary
शान्ता मन्थरेव प्रसरति
your calm, slow gait spreads like a churning motion
सु-शिखा-समूहः शोभनः केश-कलापस् ते
your hair is a beautiful mass of locks
पाठान्तरे सुशिखाः शोभनान् केशान् अवकीर्यमाणान् समूहः बधानेति
in another reading, “suśikhāḥ” means beautiful locks, and “samūha” is taken with “badhāna,” “bind them as they are being loosened”
अत्र चास्तं गच्छन् सूर्य एव पतत्-पतङ्गः
here the setting sun itself is the bouncing ball
मेघ-विच्छेदो मध्य-विषादः तारका-रूपा दृष्टिः, तम एव केशा इत्य्-आद्य्-ऊह्यम्
the break in the clouds is the drooping waist, the star-like gaze is the eyes, and darkness is the hair; the rest should be inferred
entries.literal_english: Because the words of their agitated minds do not stay on one subject: “O graceful woman, O praiseworthy one, your [playful movement] does not remain in one place”—or, in its many varied graceful motions, it excels everywhere. “A falling ball” means a ball bouncing upward. Your slender waist, burdened by your large breasts, droops and grows weary. Your calm, slow gait spreads like a churning motion. Your hair is a beautiful mass of locks. In another reading, “suśikhāḥ” means beautiful locks; “samūha” is taken with “badhāna,” “bind them as they are being loosened.” Here one should infer the imagery: the setting sun is the bouncing ball; the break in the clouds is the waist drooping; the star-like gaze is the eyes; and darkness is the hair, and so on.

entries.sanskrit: प्रहस्यात्मानम् आत्मना जिघ्रन्त्या । कान्त्या सौन्दर्येण । प्रहसनम् आत्मावघ्राणं च सौन्दर्यानुभाव-चातुर्य-विकारः ॥३८॥

कान्त्या सौन्दर्येण
“kāntyā” means by beauty
प्रहसनम् आत्मावघ्राणं च सौन्दर्यानुभाव-चातुर्य-विकारः

entries.literal_english: “Laughing, smelling herself with herself.” “Kāntyā” means by beauty. Laughter and smelling herself are transformations arising from the skill of experiencing her own beauty.

entries.literal_english: “Jyotsnām” means moonlight. They were those very groups of Gandharvas and others. Viśvāvasu was the foremost, the leader among them.

entries.sanskrit: आत्मनस् तन्द्रिणा आलस्येन । तांश् च मुक्त-केशान् वीक्ष्य नेत्रे निमीलितवान् ॥४०॥
word_for_word: आत्मनस् तन्द्रिणा आलस्येन
“by his own drowsiness” means through his own languor
तांश् च मुक्त-केशान् वीक्ष्य
seeing them with their hair loosened
नेत्रे निमीलितवान्
he closed his eyes
entries.literal_english: “By his own drowsiness” means through his own languor. Seeing them with their hair loosened, he closed his eyes.

entries.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणां विक्लेदः स्रावो यया तां निद्रां प्रचक्षते । येनेन्द्रिय-विक्लेदेन हेतुनोच्छिष्टांश् च सतो धर्षयन्ति भ्रान्तान् कुर्वन्ति । तं भूतादि-गणम् उन्मादं प्रचक्षते । तन्द्रा-जृम्भिकानिक्रोन्माद-हेतुत्वेन भूतादीनां तनूनां च चातुर्विध्यम् उक्तम् ॥४१॥
word_for_word: इन्द्रियाणां विक्लेदः स्रावो यया तां निद्रां प्रचक्षते
that condition in which there is a discharge from the senses is called sleep
येनेन्द्रिय-विक्लेदेन हेतुनोच्छिष्टांश् च सतो धर्षयन्ति भ्रान्तान् कुर्वन्ति
through that discharge of the senses, as its cause, they assail those who are impure and make them deluded
तं भूतादि-गणम् उन्मादं प्रचक्षते
that group of Bhūtas and related beings is called madness
तन्द्रा-जृम्भिकानिक्रोन्माद-हेतुत्वेन भूतादीनां तनूनां च चातुर्विध्यम् उक्तम्
the fourfold character of their forms is stated because they cause drowsiness, yawning, [the source’s unclear term] and madness
entries.literal_english: That condition in which there is a discharge from the senses is called sleep. Through that discharge of the senses, as its cause, they assail those who are impure and make them deluded. That group of Bhūtas and related beings is called madness. The fourfold character of their forms is stated because they cause drowsiness, yawning, hiccuping, and madness.

entries.sanskrit: आत्मनः सर्गो यस्मातम् । यद् येन कार्येण संप्रदानत्व-निमित्तेन । कवयः कर्म-कोविदाः । साध्येभ्यः पितृभ्यश् च स्व-पितृ-रूपेभ्यः । वितन्वते श्राद्धादिना हव्यं कव्यं च ददति ॥४३॥
word_for_word: आत्मनः सर्गो यस्मातम्
“from whom the creation of the self [arose]”—this is the reading of the text
यद् येन कार्येण संप्रदानत्व-निमित्तेन
“yat” means “for which purpose,” with the recipient relation as its cause
कवयः कर्म-कोविदाः
“kavayaḥ” means the wise, those skilled in ritual action
साध्येभ्यः पितृभ्यश् च स्व-पितृ-रूपेभ्यः
to the Sādhyas and to the Fathers, who are forms of their own fathers
वितन्वते श्राद्धादिना हव्यं कव्यं च ददति
they extend and give oblation and ancestral offering through rites such as śrāddha
entries.literal_english: “From whom the creation of the self [arose]”—this is the reading of the text. “Yat” means “for which purpose,” with the recipient relation as its cause. “Kavayaḥ” means the wise, those skilled in ritual action. To the Sādhyas and to the Fathers, who are forms of their own fathers, they extend and give the oblation and ancestral offering through rites such as śrāddha.

entries.sanskrit: प्रत्यात्म्येन प्रतिबिम्बेन । आत्माभासं प्रतिबिम्बम् आत्मनात्मनो मानः प्रतिबिम्ब-दर्शिनः सुन्दरस्य शिरः-कम्पादि-चेष्टा । अत एव तत्-सृष्टानां मिथः संमाननेन नित्यं मिथुनी-भवः ॥४५॥
word_for_word: प्रत्यात्म्येन प्रतिबिम्बेन
“pratyātmyena” means by reflection
आत्माभासं प्रतिबिम्बम्
“ātmābhāsam” means a reflection
आत्मनात्मनो मानः प्रतिबिम्ब-दर्शिनः सुन्दरस्य शिरः-कम्पादि-चेष्टा
“mānayann ātmanā ātmānam” describes the reflected one’s self-admiration: seeing his reflection, the handsome one makes gestures such as nodding his head
अत एव तत्-सृष्टानां मिथः संमाननेन नित्यं मिथुनी-भवः
therefore those created by him, mutually admiring one another, are continually paired as couples
entries.literal_english: “Pratyātmyena” means by reflection. “Ātmābhāsam” means a reflection. “Mānayann ātmanā ātmānam” describes the reflected one’s self-admiration: seeing his reflection, the handsome one makes gestures such as nodding his head. Therefore those created by him, mutually admiring one another, are continually paired as couples.

entries.sanskrit: भोग आभोगो विस्तारः पादादि-प्रसरणं तद्वता देहेन । अनुपचिते वृद्धिम् अप्राप्ते । तत् भोग-क्रोधादि-युक्तम् ॥४७॥
word_for_word: भोग आभोगो विस्तारः पादादि-प्रसरणं तद्वता देहेन
“bhoga” means a coil or expansion, the extension of the feet and so forth; “bhogavat” means possessing such a body
अनुपचिते वृद्धिम् अप्राप्ते
“anupacite” means not yet grown or increased
तत् भोग-क्रोधादि-युक्तम्
that body was endowed with a coil, anger, and the like
entries.literal_english: “Bhoga” means a coil or expansion, the extension of the feet and so forth; “bhogavat” means possessing such a body. “Anupacite” means not yet grown or increased. That body was endowed with a coil, anger, and the like.

entries.sanskrit: अमुतोऽमुष्माद् देहाद्ये केशा अहीयन्त प्रच्युतास् तेऽहयो जाताः । प्रसर्पतः पादाद्य्-आकुञ्चनैः प्रचलतोऽमुष्मात् सर्पाः । अत एव अगा न भवन्तीति नागाः, अतिवेगवन्त इत्य् अर्थः । भोगवतो जातत्वाद् भोगेन फणेनोरुर् विस्तीर्णा कन्धरा येषाम् । सर्वे चैते तत्-क्रोध-योगात् क्रूराः । तेषाम् अवान्तर-जाति-भेदः सर्प-सिद्धान्ते प्रसिद्धः ॥४८॥
word_for_word: अमुतोऽमुष्माद् देहाद्ये केशा अहीयन्त प्रच्युतास् तेऽहयो जाताः
“from this body” means from that body: the hairs that fell away became snakes
प्रसर्पतः पादाद्य्-आकुञ्चनैः प्रचलतोऽमुष्मात् सर्पाः
“crawling” means moving by contracting the feet and the like; serpents [came] from that moving body
अत एव अगा न भवन्तीति नागाः, अतिवेगवन्त इत्य् अर्थः
because they do not walk they are called nāgas; that is, they are exceedingly swift
भोगवतो जातत्वाद् भोगेन फणेनोरुर् विस्तीर्णा कन्धरा येषाम्
since they arose from the coiled body, they have broad necks with coils in the form of hoods
सर्वे चैते तत्-क्रोध-योगात् क्रूराः
all of them are fierce because of their connection with his anger
तेषाम् अवान्तर-जाति-भेदः सर्प-सिद्धान्ते प्रसिद्धः
the subdivisions of their species are well known in the treatise on snakes
entries.literal_english: “From this body” means from that body: the hairs that fell away became snakes. “Crawling” means moving by contracting the feet and the like; the snakes came from that moving body. Because they do not walk, they are called nāgas; that is, they are exceedingly swift. Since they arose from the body possessing coils, they have broad necks, with coils in the form of hoods. All of them are fierce because of their connection with his anger. The subdivisions of their species are well known in the treatise on snakes.

entries.sanskrit: ते त्वया यत् कृतं तत् सुकृतम् । सुकृतत्वम् आहुः । यस्मिन् मनु-सर्गे । क्रिया अग्निहोत्राद्याः । अतोऽस्मिन् सर्वे वयं साकं सहान्नं हविर्भागाद्य् अदाम भक्षयाम । हे ब्रह्मन् ॥५१॥
word_for_word: ते त्वया यत् कृतं तत् सुकृतम्
what you did is meritorious
सुकृतत्वम् आहुः
they call it meritorious
यस्मिन् मनु-सर्गे
“in which” means in that creation of Manu
क्रिया अग्निहोत्राद्याः

अतोऽस्मिन् सर्वे वयं साकं सहान्नं हविर्भागाद्य् अदाम भक्षयाम
therefore we all partake together of food, including the shares of oblation and the like
हे ब्रह्मन्
“O Brahmā”—this is the address
entries.literal_english: “What you did is meritorious”; they call it meritorious. “In which” means in that creation of Manu. “Kriyā” means rites such as the Agnihotra. Therefore in that creation we all partake together of food, including the shares of oblation. “O Brahmā”—this is the address.

entries.sanskrit: काय-सृष्टिम् उक्त्वा ऋषीणां सृष्टिम् आह---तपसेति । विद्या उपासना । योगोऽत्रासनादिः । सु-समाधिर् वैराग्यैश्वर्यादि-युक्तः समाधिः तेन च युक्तः । हृषीकेशः स्व-वशेन्द्रियः सन् । ऋषीर् ब्रह्मा ऋषीन् प्रजाः ससर्ज ॥५२॥
word_for_word: काय-सृष्टिम् उक्त्वा ऋषीणां सृष्टिम् आह---तपसेति
having spoken of bodily creation, he describes the creation of the sages with “tapasā”
विद्या उपासना
“vidyā” means worship
योगोऽत्रासनादिः
here “yoga” means postures and the like
सु-समाधिर् वैराग्यैश्वर्यादि-युक्तः समाधिः तेन च युक्तः
“well-concentrated” means concentration joined with renunciation, powers, and so forth, and [Brahmā] was also endowed with that
हृषीकेशः स्व-वशेन्द्रियः सन्
“Hṛṣīkeśa” means master of his own senses; being thus
ऋषीर् ब्रह्मा ऋषीन् प्रजाः ससर्ज
the seer Brahmā created the sages as his offspring
entries.literal_english: Having spoken of bodily creation, he now describes the creation of the sages: “tapasā” and the following words. “Vidyā” means worship. Here “yoga” means postures and the like. “Well-concentrated” means concentration joined with renunciation, powers, and so forth, and [Brahmā] was also endowed with that. “Hṛṣīkeśa” means master of his own senses. Being thus, the seer Brahmā created the sages as his offspring.

entries.sanskrit: किं तद् देहं यस्यांशम् अदाद् इत्य् अत आह---यद् इति । समाधिश् च योगश् च ऋद्धिश् च ऐश्वर्यं तपश् च विद्या च विरक्तिश् च विद्यन्ते यस्मिंस् तत् ॥५३॥
word_for_word: किं तद् देहं यस्यांशम् अदाद् इत्य् अत आह---यद् इति
“What is that body of which he gave a portion?” To this he answers with “yat”
समाधिश् च योगश् च ऋद्धिश् च ऐश्वर्यं
concentration, yoga, and prosperity—that is, supernatural power
तपश् च विद्या च विरक्तिश् च विद्यन्ते यस्मिंस् तत्
austerity, knowledge, and detachment are present in that body
entries.literal_english: “What is that body of which he gave a portion?” To this he answers with “yat.” That is the body in which concentration, yoga, prosperity—that is, supernatural power—austerity, knowledge, and detachment are present.
